code='''from collections import Counter, deque

def _components(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            color = grid[r][c]
            if color in seen or (r, c) in set():
                pass
            if (r, c) in seen:
                continue
            seen.add((r, c))
            q = [(r, c)]
            cells = []
            while q:
                y, x = q.pop()
                cells.append((y, x))
                for yy, xx in ((y-1,x),(y+1,x),(y,x-1),(y,x+1)):
                    if 0 <= yy < h and 0 <= xx < w and (yy,xx) not in seen and grid[yy][xx] == color:
                        seen.add((yy,xx)); q.append((yy,xx))
            out.append((color, cells))
    return out

def _shape(cells):
    r0=min(r for r,c in cells); c0=min(c for r,c in cells)
    return frozenset((r-r0,c-c0) for r,c in cells)

def transform(grid):
    g=[row[:] for row in grid]
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    counts=Counter(v for row in g for v in row)
    bg=Counter(v for row in g for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    comps=[(color,cells,_shape(cells)) for color,cells in _components(g) if color != bg]
    # If two differently colored objects have exactly the same silhouette, make
    # the less represented color agree with the more represented one.
    for i,(ca,aa,sa) in enumerate(comps):
        for cb,bb,sb in comps[i+1:]:
            if ca != cb and sa == sb:
                # Prefer the color with more total cells in the grid.
                target = ca if counts[ca] >= counts[cb] else cb
                chosen = bb if target == ca else aa
                source = cb if target == ca else ca
                for r,c in chosen: g[r][c]=target
                return g
    return g
'''
